name: Marshal's Anthem
oracle_text:
Multikicker {1}{W} (You may pay an additional {1}{W} any number of times as you cast this spell.)
Creatures you control get +1/+1.
When this enchantment enters, return up to X target creature cards from your graveyard to the battlefield, where X is the number of times this enchantment was kicked.
blocked_sentences: When this enchantment enters, return up to X target creature cards from your graveyard to the battlefield, where X is the number of times this enchantment was kicked.

needs.what: A target spec whose number of targets is a value expression rather than a literal -- `count: {"additional_paid": true}` (or any `value_keys` entry) plus an "up to" reading, so the caster picks between zero and X targets at announcement and X is computed when the ability goes on the stack. Concretely: TargetModel.count in src/automtg/cards/schema.py is `int | Literal["any"]`, and engine/targeting.py branches on `spec.count == "any"` / `spec.count > 1` with the literal integer; both need to accept an evaluated amount, and the combination enumeration needs to offer every size from 0..X rather than exactly X
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The two spellings `reference` offers are both a different card. `count: "any"` is "any number of target creature cards", which unbinds the count from the kicker entirely -- Marshal's Anthem cast with no kicks would reanimate the whole graveyard for {2}{W}{W}. `count: N` is a number written into the card, and `optional: true` on top of it means "exactly N or none", forbidding every size between 1 and N-1, so neither can say "up to X". Moving the choice to resolution does not rescue it either: a selector's `count` *does* accept a value expression (selectors.pick_from_pool calls evaluate_value on it), so `return_from_graveyard` with `objects: {count: {"additional_paid": true}}` computes the right number -- but that is untargeted (no legality check at announcement, no fizzle when the cards leave, and `becomes_target` never fires) and it sets min_count == max_count, forcing *exactly* X rather than up to X. `value_keys.additional_paid` already supplies X correctly here -- `cast_additional` is set in game.py at cast time and lives on the object, which survives the zone change onto the battlefield, so a `self_enters` trigger reads it -- so the missing piece is only the target *count*, not the value
